summary: Plan for COST-EXPERIMENTS: five experiments (E1 C1-retrospective, E2 context profile, E3 model routing, E4 pruning, E5 criteria injection), each with acceptance number+predicate+units, a null control, G1/G2/G3 checks, a named one-step reversal with tripwire, the instrument reused by path, and a model recommendation on the decidability axis.
next_step: Plan critic (BLOCKING/CARRIED, bounded at two exchanges, no browser). Do not build.
blockers: COST-INSTRUMENT must land tools/cost.mjs -> docs/data/cost-ledger.json before E3/E4/E5 can take a before-number. E1/E2 need only the instrument's transcript parser.

G1 baseline unresolved: mean concurrent agents 4.40 over the 62.1h wall-clock span (5.3 over COST-INSTRUMENT's 52 active hours), peak 16, against a floor of 12. Flagged for COST-INSTRUMENT to rule; every G1 predicate in the plan is conditional on it.
key_findings: COST.md section 2 measured the WRONG FILE. The *.jsonl glob matches only the orchestrator's main thread (isSidechain=false throughout, zero Sonnet). Fleet transcripts are in <session>/subagents/ - ~405 agent-<id>.jsonl files with agent-<id>.meta.json sidecars whose 'description' field is the dispatch headline and the attribution key the programme needs.

SELF-CORRECTION: my first pass double-counted. Deduplicating on requestId removes 39,245 priced requests carrying 6.90 Btok of cache_read. Corrected all-in spend ~$5,887 (subagents $5,346.01), against COST-INSTRUMENT's independently derived $5,792.69 at db449a5. COST-INSTRUMENT's figure is the one of record; the instrument owns cost (rule 10). Every qualitative conclusion survived the correction because all of them are ratios.

cache_read is 81.6% of subagent spend ($4,362.72). cache_write 5m 17.3%, output 1.0%, uncached input 0.1%. Cache HIT RATIO is already 98.3% - the lever is not the ratio, it is context_size x request_count. OUTPUT IS 1% OF SPEND: 'make agents write less' targets a rounding error.

Cost is roughly QUADRATIC in tool calls: mean cost per agent $4.55 -> $51.83 from the 0-99 to the 300-399 request bin (a ~3.5x rise in requests buys ~11x cost), and per-request cost itself nearly doubles. Largest agent traced: context grows near-linearly 23,757 -> 578,648 tokens over 314 requests, sum/(n*max)=0.658. Absent from COST.md section 4 and from the research ranking.

RULING C1 MEASURES AS INERT. First-request cache_write is 2.0% of all cache_write = 0.32% of spend (ceiling, vs a 2% bar). Tight bursts warm_fraction 0.958 vs staggered 0.965 (+0.7pp, vs a 10pp bar). 378/403 agents already read cache on their first request. Expected verdict: revert per C1's own tripwire - but the builder must reproduce independently, not confirm.

COST.md section 2's 'essentially all Opus, 3230 vs 29' is main-thread-only. Fleet is 42,893 Opus requests / 368 agents vs 3,089 Sonnet / 35 agents - Sonnet is already 6.7% of requests and 2.4% of spend. Routing's ceiling is the 2.5x price ratio (1.67x after the Sonnet intro rate ends 2026-08-31), so the 25% bar CANNOT be reached by routing alone.

COST.md section 6.1's example prices are 3x the real rate (input 15 vs 5, output 75 vs 25). Ratios right, absolutes look Opus-4.1-era. Also the schema omits the cache-write TTL split: usage.cache_creation carries ephemeral_5m and ephemeral_1h separately, priced 1.25x and 2x. Subagent 1h writes are zero; the orchestrator's are not, and it is in scope.
